craft_claim: Suspense requires granting the audience anticipation of impending crisis, whereas surprise withholds knowledge until the impact moment.

supporting_evidence.note: King argues that suspense grows from putting sympathetic characters in agonizing predicaments where readers dread what is coming.
McKee differentiates suspense (curiosity with emotional investment over time) from sudden shock or surprise.
Audience knows Oedipus is the killer; suspense comes entirely from watching him dig his own grave.

scope: Thrillers, horror, mysteries, and dramatic narrative pacing.
exceptions: Whodunit mysteries where identity of culprit is concealed until detective's climactic gathering.
